abstract.para: Understand how CPU partitioning and affinity are configured with &systemd; resource control and taskset when cset is not available.

section.title: Using &systemd; instead of cset
section.para: In earlier product releases, the cset utility managed cpusets and CPU shielding. cset supports the cpuset controller only on the cgroups v1 hierarchy. On systems with the unified cgroups v2 hierarchy, the cpuset controller is used through &systemd; control configurations (such as AllowedCPUs) instead.

section.title: CPU affinity and task management tools
section.para: The following tools and settings are used to configure CPU shielding and real-time process execution:

listitem.para: Configures persistent or transient CPU allocation for slices, services and workloads with the AllowedCPUs= property. To completely shield these CPUs from general system tasks, you must also explicitly exclude them from the primary system slices (such as system.slice and user.slice).
Retrieves or sets the CPU affinity of a process, binding running tasks to specific logical CPUs.
Sets the real-time scheduling policy (SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR) and priority of a task.
